PI:  Research will focus on understanding the genomic mechanisms underlying lineage establishment, persistence, adaptation, and extinction in highly inbred populations inhabiting urban environments. The successful candidate will address questions at the interface of evolutionary genetics, population genomics, and urban ecology, with broad implications for our understanding of adaptation in anthropogenic ecosystems and the evolution of economically important pest species. 
Current research themes include insecticide resistance evolution over historic to contemporary time frames, population genomics across socioeconomic landscapes, and the heritability of stress induced epigenetic marks. A variety of next-generation sequencing approaches may be employed, including ddRADseq, whole genome sequencing, targeted sequence capture, and other emerging genomic technologies.

column9: 1) Anyone understand why this has a tax free salary? 2) Some Postdocs are funded this way in Sweden with tax free salary usually from a specific funder. They tend to be be around the same amount as how much a Postdoc would make after taxes. 3) I have been offered positions like this before and was encouraged to decline them due to substandard employment rights. You aren't eligible for vacation, retirement, transit discounts, and don't accumulate residency time e.g. for citizenship. Avoid avoid avoid unless you are positively desprate. Some discourse on this here. https://www.reddit.com/r/postdoc/comments/1szzwnq/swedish_postdoc_scholarship/  4) PI here. I came to Sweden from the US on the same type of postdoc stipend and it worked well for me. We of course want and expect the postdoc to take the standard vacation time (usually about 30 days, depending on your age). And stipend postdocs get public health insurance because it’s guaranteed to anyone residing in Sweden for more than one year. However, it’s true that stipend positions don’t get retirement, paid parental leave, or paid sick leave. That said, a benefit of stipend postdoc positions is that it can provide a pathway to extend the postdoctoral “time” in Sweden until you secure your own grant and then become permanently employed as a researcher (as I did). And my stipend postdoc time did count towards residency for citizenship. Overall, the stipend postdoc worked well for me but I recognize that it may not work for all situations. If you have questions or want a full explanation of the stipend postdoc situation, please email me stefan.hupperts@slu.se 5) I came to Sweden for a postdoc (although not this exact type) and the lifestyle was a wonderful change from the US. The culture of taking rest, holidays, and vacation seriously was a huge eye-opener. Plus this seems like a really cool project—my two cents/.2 kronor! 6) Also moved from the US to Sweden with a similar type of funding, and it was great. Sweden has many funding options that you can plan to transition to later (e.g., VR our FORMAS) as well, so it can be a good opportunity.
